subject: KV eviction cascade / 99th pct latency spike — exclusion request
messages:
From: Priya Menon <priya.menon@atlascloud.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 22:50:00 -0700
Subject: High tail latency during scheduled window (requesting SLA apportionment)

Hi Connor,

We observed a sustained p95/p99 latency spike on Redwood's /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings endpoints between 2026-11-03T21:42:00Z and 2026-11-03T22:05:00Z that coincides with what your status page lists as a third-party maintenance event for your managed KV provider. During that ~23-minute window our service saw 3–5x increases in request latency and several request failures that forced us to fallback to a cheaper model (resulting in additional app-side throttling).

We provisioned the environment to your recommended throughput and didn't see any capacity issues on our side. Our traces show repeated cold starts and increased token-generation latency, consistent with a cache eviction cascade. The SLA states that third-party maintenance may be excluded, but the language also requires notice and that the degradation be limited to components outside Redwood's control. We did not receive advance notice about the provider maintenance from Redwood, and the impact appears broader than a single shard.

Please provide:
- Your timeline for the event (start/end) as recorded in Redwood logs
- Any probe/edge logs showing upstream errors or cache misses for our account (Atlas Cloud)
- Your proposed apportionment for uptime credits (we expect an explanation of whether the third-party exclusion applies and how you calculated the credit)

Attached is a sample of our latency measurements and a couple of trace IDs: trace-7a2c, trace-7a2d.

We'd like to get this resolved quickly — this incident affected a near-real-time feature on our checkout flow.

Thanks,
Priya
Ops Lead, Atlas Cloud

From: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
To: Priya Menon <priya.menon@atlascloud.com>
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High tail latency during scheduled window (requesting SLA apportionment)

Hi Priya — thanks for the report and for including traces. We're digging in and I wanted to acknowledge receipt and share next steps.

Preliminary timeline from our control plane:
- 2026-11-03T21:40:12Z — downstream KV provider started a maintenance rollout in eu-west-1 that included forced TTL compaction on several host groups.
- 2026-11-03T21:41:05Z — our routing layer detected increase in cold cache misses and started rerouting to warm hosts; cache warming took ~9–12 minutes for affected shards.
- 2026-11-03T22:05:40Z — token-generation latencies returned to baseline for most requests.

We're 1) collecting the SRE audit logs for the affected shard group and 2) pulling the request-level logs for your account. I'll attach the preliminary support bundle in the next message.

Short answer on exclusion: our SLA allows exclusion for documented third-party maintenance when the event is documented and we provided reasonable notice. At present, we did not surface the KV provider's internal maintenance schedule proactively (that's on us), so I want to handle this carefully.

Assigning Jordan and Grace to validate the apportionment math and confirm whether the impact is isolated to the KV layer or cascaded into model serving. Marissa, want to weigh in on an interim credit offer while we finish the audit?

Connor O'Brien
Technical Account Manager — Redwood Inference

From: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
To: Priya Menon <priya.menon@atlascloud.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High tail latency during scheduled window (requesting SLA apportionment)

Hi Priya — attaching our initial support bundle (support-bundle-connor_20261104.tar.gz) that includes: router traces for the timeframe, cache-miss counters, and host-level CPU/IO summaries.

Attachment stubs: 
- support-bundle-connor_20261104.tar.gz (router-traces/ cache-miss CSV / host-summaries.txt)
- atlas_latency_sample_20261103.csv (the sample you provided, echoed for record)

Based on early analysis, the most defensible apportionment is to treat this as a mixed-impact event: 
- KV provider forced compaction caused elevated cold cache miss rate (primary cause)
- Routing and model-serving experienced transient latency amplification while caches warmed (secondary)

Proposed interim credit: 25% credit for the affected 23-minute window while we complete a deeper audit. If the audit shows the impact was primarily within the KV provider (and we can document the provider's maintenance), we will apply the third-party exclusion and issue a partial credit consistent with our SLA terms. If the audit shows Redwood routing/serving contributed materially beyond the KV hits, we'll increase the credit accordingly.

If that interim approach isn't acceptable, let me know and we'll escalate to legal/product immediately.

Connor

From: Priya Menon <priya.menon@atlascloud.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@atlascloud.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 10:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High tail latency during scheduled window (requesting SLA apportionment)

Connor — thanks for the quick reply and the bundle. A couple of clarifications/questions: 

1) We disagree with the characterization that this was primarily a provider compaction. Our traces show repeated request replays from your SDK as the client retried failures, which multiplied the load on the serving tier. That looks like a combination of your client-side retry policy and routing behavior.

2) We did not get any notice about the provider maintenance from Redwood or the provider. Per our contract, third-party exclusion only applies if Redwood provided prior notice or the event is an upstream outage that you can demonstrate was isolated to a provider component.

3) We are open to an interim credit but 25% is low given the 23-minute duration and the impact to checkout. Requesting 50% pending full audit.

Please include the raw SDK logs/redwood-client-retry events for our account and the exact host/instance identifiers for the affected shards. We'll review as soon as we have them.

If you can escalate to get those additional artifacts today, we can avoid a formal escalation.

-Priya

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Menon <priya.menon@atlascloud.com>
Cc: connor.obrien@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, legal@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High tail latency during scheduled window (requesting SLA apportionment)

Hi Priya — Marissa here (Head of Customer Reliability). First, I want to apologize for the customer experience — that level of latency during checkout is unacceptable and I appreciate you bringing the traces.

We're escalating this as follows:
- SRE will run a targeted replay against the affected shard group and produce a deterministic timeline (we'll include host IDs and SDK retry logs).
- Legal will review the SLA exclusion requirements and confirm whether lack of notice disqualifies the provider exclusion for this event.
- I am authorizing an elevated interim credit of 50% for the 23-minute window while we complete the audit. We can revisit the final apportionment after the audit but we want to make sure Atlas Cloud is made whole quickly for the customer impact.

I'll follow up with the SRE report and the raw artifacts (host IDs, router logs, SDK client logs) by end of day tomorrow. If that timeline is acceptable, we'll mark the ticket HUBSPOT-27391 as high priority.

Sincerely,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

--
Marissa Cole
Redwood Inference
Attachments: none (support bundle and csv included earlier)
